doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Jazz and rock banned as music of the enemy
summary: Western music like Beatles, Miles Davis and Dizzy was prohibited and listeners could be jailed.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Sometimes. Most of the time anything coming from the Western countries, like the Beatles, Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Dizzy Gillespie. That was the music of the enemy and the ideology back then was that the enemy was trying to penetrate our ideology any way possible. So music was one of the ways to penetrate our socialist ideology. So yes it was prohibited many times, it was prohibited to play music, you got in trouble for listening to the music. The only times we were able to play, once in a blue moon was when the government wanted to show, for some reason, that they were open about the music of the United States, just when it was for their convenience. Otherwise we went through a lot of hurdles, we got in trouble and even people went to jail for listening and dancing to Beatles music or Rolling Stones, so forth and so on.
